title: State v. Emmett Sayle
teaser: On their twentieth anniversary, a woman falls from a coastal lookout at dusk. Her husband was the only one there. He says the railing gave way.
summary: Lorna Sayle, 49, fell 70 feet from the Kestrel Point lookout at dusk on October 12, her twentieth wedding anniversary. Her husband Emmett, 52, a land surveyor, says she leaned on the railing to take a photograph and it gave way, and that he climbed down to try to reach her. The state says there was no accident: that he pushed his wife, and took his time reporting it.

evidence.label: The railing
evidence.detail: A section of railing tore loose with her. A parks report four months earlier flagged corroded bolts and was never acted on. An engineer says it would have failed under a hard lean or a shove, and can't say which.

evidence.label: The nineteen minutes
evidence.detail: Lorna's last photo was taken at 6:41 PM. Emmett's 911 call came at 7:00 PM. He says he climbed down at once and had no signal. Network maps show one bar at the lookout and on the upper path.

evidence.label: The life insurance
evidence.detail: Lorna's cover rose from $250,000 to $600,000 eight months before her death. Both spouses raised theirs on the same day, on their broker's advice.

evidence.label: The affair
evidence.detail: Emmett had been seeing a colleague for a year. Lorna found the messages in September and booked a first appointment with a divorce lawyer for October 15.

evidence.label: The scratches
evidence.detail: Emmett had fresh scratches on both forearms. He says they came from the rocks. Scrapings under Lorna's nails held a trace of his DNA, which the lab calls unremarkable in a married couple.

evidence.label: The boots
evidence.detail: Mud on Emmett's boots matches the cliff path, which supports his climb. It stops at the second ledge, well short of where she lay.

evidence.label: The autopsy
evidence.detail: Her injuries fit a fall. She landed 11 feet out from the cliff, which an expert says suits a stumble or a push equally. The medical examiner believes she lived for some minutes after landing.

evidence.label: The last photo
evidence.detail: The final image on her phone is a blurred smear of sky at 6:41 PM. It fits a camera jolted by a failing railing, and it fits a camera knocked from her hand.

witnesses.name: Paul Dunmore
witnesses.statement: Was a quarter of a mile away on a windy evening. Heard a woman cry out. He thinks she said 'Don't.' It could have been 'Oh.' He told police both.

witnesses.name: Bridget Noone
witnesses.statement: Says Lorna told her a week before: 'He's being so kind lately, it frightens me.' She also says Lorna insisted on the anniversary walk herself, as a last try.

witnesses.name: Hannah Pell
witnesses.statement: Says Emmett told her he'd 'be free by Christmas.' She took that to mean the divorce. She ended it with him the day Lorna died.

witnesses.name: Ivo Lennart
witnesses.statement: Wrote the railing report and says the bolts could have gone any day. Found Emmett at the cliff top at 7:40, soaked and shaking, and says he could barely speak.

points.claim: Nineteen minutes passed before he called for help
There was a bar of signal, so 'no signal' is a lie
She had a divorce lawyer booked three days later
He stood to collect $600,000
He told his lover he'd be free by Christmas
His DNA was under her nails and his arms were scratched
A woman was heard crying 'Don't'
She told her sister his kindness frightened her
The mud stops at the second ledge, so he never reached her
A man who cheats for a year will do anything to get out
The parks report warned of those bolts four months earlier
The ranger says those bolts could have gone any day
Nobody can tell a hard lean from a shove
Eleven feet out fits a stumble as well as a push
The mud proves he really did climb down
Married people carry each other's DNA, and rocks scratch arms
They both raised their cover, on the broker's advice
A quarter mile in wind, and it might have been 'Oh'
It was Lorna who insisted on that walk
'Free by Christmas' fits a divorce just as well
The ranger found him soaked, shaking and unable to speak
She was taking a photo when it happened, just as he says

fixations.1: The clock: 6:41, 7:00, 7:40. Nineteen minutes has to be accounted for, step by step.
fixations.2: Whoever spoke last and sounded sure.
fixations.3: A man who cheats on his wife for a year and then gets rich when she dies.
fixations.4: Probabilities: how often railings fail, and how often wives die three days before a divorce meeting.
fixations.5: The body. You know what a 70-foot fall does, and how long someone can last.
fixations.6: Corroded bolts. You've seen what the sea air does to metal, and you know how often the report gets ignored.
fixations.8: One word, across a quarter mile of wind, and what a mind does with it afterwards.
fixations.9: A man who could barely speak, and a woman who was frightened by kindness.
fixations.10: The affair. A man like that has already shown you what his promises are worth.
fixations.11: The negligence of a park that was warned, and what the state must prove about a shove nobody saw.

record.reason: He had reasons to want her gone, and his nineteen minutes were never properly explained. But the railing had been reported as unsafe, nobody could tell a lean from a shove, and every physical fact fit a fall as well as it fit a push. Suspicion was all the state had. It never proved he laid a hand on her.

beats: Emmett Sayle did not push his wife.
She leaned out to get the light on the water, the way she always did. The bolts let go. It was exactly what he said.
He did climb down. He got as far as the second ledge, and from there he could see her.
She was alive. She had lifted one hand. She was saying his name.
He had his phone out. There was one bar of signal where he stood.
He sat down on the ledge.
He thought about October 15, and about Christmas. He stayed there, holding the phone, until she stopped.
Then he dialled. By the time the ranger found him he was shaking, and that was real too.
truth.closing: You were asked whether he pushed her. He did not.
